units.translation: 17 sch. a is placed after b in P | 18 συμπεπλευκέναι in P : σὺν in L | 19 ὅτι — Ἀπολλωνίῳ in L : ἰστέον δὲ ὅτι Φ. μὲν συμφ. Ἀπ. λέγοντι Ἀλκιμέδην μητέρα εἶναι Ἰάσονος τὴν Φυλάκου θυγατέρα in P | 21 Πολυμήδην from Apollonius or Πολυμήλην from the Homeric scholia, Ruhnken | 22 Αἴσονος καὶ Θεογνήτης τῆς Λ. (the rest supplied by W) in L : Θεογνήτην τὴν θυγατέρα Λ. μητέρα Ἰάσονος γεγονέναι φησίν in P
Theognete, daughter of Laodicus, (he says Jason was the son).
b. Hesiod (fr. 117 Rz.²) says that Iphiclus ran over wheat ears, but Demarete (42 fr. 1 J.) says over the sea. He is the son of Phylacus and Clymene, daughter of Minyas.
1 the first sentence of scholion b follows the second in P | 3 Hyginus, Fabulae 14 (44, 17 Schm.)
2 πύρινων ἀθέρων in P : -ους -ας in L : -ης -ος in H | 3 Δημαρέτης in L : -άρετος in P : -άρατος F. cf. W, Hermes 66, 1931, 466 | υἱὸς in P : τῆς in L
c. The figure is antiphrasis. Instead of “swiftly Iphiclus came”: “he did not remain long in Phylace.”
d. 〈μήτρως:〉 uncle. Lgr
5 sch. c is read after a in L, in P inserted after Ἀργοναύταις in sch. a
e. “For he married his sister”: through the attendant circumstance he indicates the preceding action.

f. 〈ὄπυιεν:〉 “he had married”: either the word is formed from ὠπή, that is, “eyes”; or from ὄπτω and ἐπιτηρῶ, “I watch”; or from ὄψ, “voice,” because of the conversations of men with women, from which also women are called ὄαροι (I 327).
10 sch. ABT Σ 383
10 W separated this scholion from the preceding one | 11 ἢ ἀπὸ τοῦ in P : ὁ in L | ὄπτω καὶ ἐπιτηρῶ W : ὀπτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηρῶν in L : ὀπῶ τὸ ἐπιτηρῶ in P
48 a. 〈πηοσύνη:〉 kinship. Lg.
b. This kinship urged him. Lmr
16 Apollodorus, Bibliotheca I 104
49 a. “Nor in Pherae did Admetus...”: Pherae was named after Pheres, son of Cretheus, the father of Admetus.
16 sch. B B 591
16 A. added “a city in Macedonia” after Φεραὶ. cf. W 29
b. 〈ἐυρρήνεσσι:〉 those having fine sheep. Lgr
18 sch. III 1086
18 ταῖς — ἐχούσαις W : τῶν — ἐχόντων
c. ἐυρρήνεσσι instead of πολυπροβάτοις, “rich in sheep.” P
50. The Chalcodonian mountain above Pherae. Lg (P)

51–52. “Nor did they remain in Alope”: a city of Thessaly or Magnesia. πολυλήιοι either from λήιον, that is, “corn-bearing plain,” or from λεία, “booty,” which is better; for he adds “well skilled in wiles.” They are said to be sleepless, clever, and enduring.
53. 〈γνωτός:〉 instead of “brother.” Lg
54–55 a. Aethalides: a proper name. He is the son of Hermes and Eupolemeia, daughter of Myrmidon.
1 Hyginus, Fabulae 14 (44, 23 Schm.)
1 ὄνομα κύριον Lg; P added “having the form of a patronymic” after κύριον, omitting the rest
b. Amphryssus is also written with β, as Dionysius (32 fr. 12 J.) says. It is a river of Thessaly. It is accented on the antepenult, as in the eighth book of the Katholike (Herodian I 213, 16 L.).
